draft.title: Filtration, decantation and magnets
card: Filtration
A mixture is poured through filter paper. The tiny holes let liquid through, but catch solid pieces that have not dissolved. The liquid that passes through is called the filtrate.
Decantation
Leave a mixture to stand so the solid settles to the bottom. Then carefully pour the liquid off the top and leave the solid behind.
Magnet
A magnet pulls out iron from a mixture, such as iron filings mixed with sand. Sand is not attracted, so it stays behind.

Each method works because of a difference between the parts of the mixture. Filtration and decantation separate an undissolved solid from a liquid. A solid that has dissolved cannot be caught this way.
draft.remember: Match the method to the difference: size and settling for solids in liquid, magnetism for iron.

a.q: Sand and water are shaken together in a jar. Which method separates the sand from the water by catching the sand?
opts: Filtration
Magnet
Decantation, without letting it settle
Pouring the mixture onto a magnet
a.why: Filter paper holds back undissolved sand and lets the water through. A magnet does not work because sand is not attracted to it.
a.clue: Which method uses paper with tiny holes?

b.q: Priya has a jar of salt dissolved in water. She wants to remove the salt using filter paper. What happens?
opts: The salt passes through with the water
The salt is caught in the filter paper
The salt is pulled out by a magnet
The salt settles and can be poured off
b.why: Dissolved salt is spread through the water in tiny particles, so it passes through the holes in the filter paper with the water. Filtration only catches solids that have not dissolved, which is why the tempting answer of catching the salt is wrong.
b.clue: Is dissolved salt a solid piece that can be caught?

b.best: The salt passes through with the water

a.q: Before decanting muddy water, Sam leaves the jar to stand for an hour. Why does he wait?
opts: So the mud settles to the bottom of the jar
So the mud dissolves into the water
So the mud floats up to the top of the water
So the water soaks down into the mud
a.why: Decantation pours the liquid off the top, so the solid must first sink to the bottom and stay there. Waiting does not make the mud dissolve, and a dissolved solid would pour off with the water anyway.
a.clue: Where must the solid be when you pour the liquid off?
